hints: Focus on the colour and solubility of the silver halide precipitate, as each halogen gives a very different result with ammonia.
A precipitate soluble in dilute ammonia tells you Y must be a chloroalkane, so narrow it down to the two structures containing chlorine.
For elimination to an alkene, check for a hydrogen on the carbon next to the C-Cl carbon, since a structure with no beta-hydrogen cannot eliminate.
walkthrough:
**Use the silver nitrate test to find the halogen**

Think of this as a fingerprint test for halogenoalkanes. Warm aqueous $AgNO_3$ hydrolyses the C-X bond to give $X^-$, which forms $AgX$.

$$R-X + H_2O \rightarrow R-OH + X^- + H^+$$
$$Ag^+(aq) + X^-(aq) \rightarrow AgX(s)$$

**Recall the colours and ammonia solubility**

Your friendly memory aid is: chloride is white and dissolves in dilute $NH_3$, bromide is cream and needs concentrated $NH_3$, iodide is yellow and stays insoluble.

$$AgCl(s) + 2NH_3(aq) \rightarrow [Ag(NH_3)_2]^+(aq) + Cl^-(aq)$$

**Conclude Y is a chloroalkane**

Since the precipitate dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia, it must be white $AgCl$. So Y contains chlorine, which leaves only the two chloroalkane skeletal structures.

**Apply the elimination condition**

Elimination of $HX$ needs a hydrogen on the adjacent (beta) carbon:
$$R-CH_2-CH_2-Cl + KOH \rightarrow R-CH=CH_2 + KCl + H_2O$$
The straight chain 1-chlorobutane, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2Cl$, has plenty of beta-hydrogens and forms but-1-ene. The branched $(CH_3)_3CCH_2Cl$ has a quaternary beta-carbon with no hydrogen, so it cannot eliminate.

options.A: This is bromoethane, $CH_3CH_2Br$. It would give cream $AgBr$, which is only soluble in concentrated ammonia, not dilute ammonia. Although it can eliminate to ethene, it fails the first test.
options.B: This is 1-iodopropane, $CH_3CH_2CH_2I$. It would give yellow $AgI$, which is insoluble even in concentrated ammonia. Although it can eliminate to propene, it fails the first test.
options.C: This is 1-chlorobutane, $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2Cl$. Hydrolysis gives $Cl^-$ which forms white $AgCl$, soluble in dilute $NH_3$. It also has beta-hydrogens on C2, so it eliminates with hot ethanolic NaOH to give but-1-ene. It passes both tests.
options.D: This is 1-chloro-2,2-dimethylpropane, $(CH_3)_3CCH_2Cl$. It passes the first test by giving white $AgCl$, but it has no hydrogen on the beta-carbon because the adjacent carbon is bonded to three methyl groups. With no beta-hydrogen, elimination to an alkene is impossible.
